# Existing-card follow-up: isolated candidate

The 13 October simulated V2 fleet run found 51 unwanted new-photo sends across 16 creators with photos. They arose when fans accepted an existing card or asked what it showed or cost. The prior card was excluded from the new-offer menu, but new files remained valid model selections. The structured schema checked only whether a chosen slot was in that menu, not whether another send had been requested. This is one shared action-selection defect, not 51 distinct defects.

## Baseline and changes

- Checked the `v2-stage345` remote head `2b59d900bd61fbcd335228f2032c6548b37535a1`; its five responsible source/test blobs match the local pre-edit files byte for byte. The open draft grounding PR #1 targets an older branch and overlaps the already deployed grounding component; none of it was merged here.
- Saved the pre-edit regression result in `existing-card-discussion-baseline.json`: 90 checks, 12 failures. In both ordinary and Business routes, each of the four fleet phrases had a new photo in its allowed choices. An absent or route-mismatched previous card also left new-photo choices. The baseline exact resend in the rig required a fresh verification stub; that fixture was corrected before this saved baseline.
- `src/turn.ts`: recognize bounded existing-card discussion only after explicit new/resend/missing requests have been considered. Such a turn supplies no new media slot. Requests for a new file still use the ordinary eligible menu; requests for the exact same photo still use fresh catalogue and ownership verification. A deictic send request now takes that existing exact-reference path instead of choosing an unrelated new file.
- `src/media.ts`: show the model the verified previous card's catalogue description and acknowledged status as context without making it selectable. If there is no scoped receipt, state that no previous photo is verified. Remaining inventory counts do not imply a new offer on this turn.
- `src/grounding.ts`: permit a supported description of this receipt-backed card in a text-only answer and reject unsupported bounded garment/colour claims using the existing guard. The normal text-only and selected-media checks remain in place.
- Changed one sentence in the shared photos paragraph and reviewed its new `riley-prompt-v11.txt` snapshot. The same renderer supplies the dashboard's displayed prompt and the runtime base prompt; the per-turn previous-card note is runtime evidence only.

## Verification and limits

The new isolated queue/structured-contract/fake-Telegram regression passes 155 checks. It covers the four fleet phrases plus short price/acceptance variants on both routes; repeated discussion; absent prior, reset and route mismatch; invalid model selection failing closed; supported versus invented previous-card description; ordinary topic change; explicit different photo; and exact resend. One model call per turn is asserted. The existing 23-script offline gate passed 23/23; TypeScript `--noEmit` and `git diff --check` passed. Focused photo-reference, delivery, payments, bundles, grounding and prompt-display tests also passed in that gate. No live chats, purchases or persistent data were changed.

An isolated real-model replay of this first candidate used 464 model requests across 17 current V2 creators with frozen catalogue/settings and fake Telegram. It removed all 51 original unwanted new-card actions, but found one different action failure: an ordinary exact resend for Trashy. The acknowledged prior photo had a blank visual description. The initial send allows a legacy blank-description file, while the existing exact-reference check rejected that same file solely because its description was blank. The bounded evidence is in `jesse98/twin-dashboard` branch `codex/v2-card-model-validation-20261013`, `docs/existing-card-candidate-results.json` and `docs/existing-card-candidate-failure-detail.json`. The model replay also recorded 25 possible visibility claims, four quoted prices, one possible false-stock claim, and two empty final replies; those flags require separate evidence review and are not counted as confirmed cases here.

The original focused candidate passed 155 checks. A new pre-edit regression is saved as `existing-card-resend-baseline.json`: 161 checks, three failed assertions about this same resend, with the acknowledged first card succeeding. In `src/turn.ts`, exact resend now permits a blank-description item already eligible for the initial send; exact creator-scoped key/path, analysis eligibility, requested-attribute match, fresh catalogue/ownership, route and epoch checks remain. No catalogue item is made newly eligible for an initial send. The updated focused test passes 165 checks, including unchanged paid price and rejection when a blank-description file cannot support a specifically requested bikini detail. TypeScript `--noEmit` and diff check pass. The 23-script offline gate had 22 passing scripts and one failure in `check-memory-wiring.ts` at its byte-identical clock-bearing system prompt check (MW08); the unchanged memory suite then passed all 177 checks on one rerun. This test compares two turns without masking the changing local clock at MW08, while its MW03 comparison does mask that clock. The original failure is retained in the stage record and is not relabelled as an original 23/23 pass.

The amended source candidate at remote commit `cae54ad62434d6f804ddb9d81b5da51e89fde506` was replayed with the same frozen fleet fixture: 464 cases, 464 conversation-model requests, 17 active V2 creators, **zero action failures**, including Trashy's blank-description exact resend. No fan messages, purchases or production writes occurred; live bot/dashboard image and active creator settings were unchanged before and after. The result is `jesse98/twin-dashboard` branch `codex/v2-card-model-validation-v2-20261013`, `docs/existing-card-candidate-v2-results.json`; bounded model text review is in `docs/existing-card-candidate-v2-flags.json` on that branch. The overlay touched only the same four source files, with the changed `src/turn.ts` SHA-256 pinned in the runner.

The text review found **separate remaining problems** despite the zero action failures: five replies asserted a particular item's Star price despite the existing prompt forbidding it; three of the eight price flags were only generic Stars conversion guidance. Four empty-final results were flagged. The subsequent raw/transport review confirmed three blank-caption cards; the fourth was Riley’s deliberately rejected transport, which correctly has no delivered reply. See `reply-outcomes-stage.md`; the original flag evidence is preserved. Some of the 31 possible visibility flags were ordinary purchase instructions, but several replies to a deliberately failed ownership/reference read asserted that the card was visible or that a free resend was impossible without verified ownership. These were not repaired by this action-selection candidate. The flag totals are heuristic and overlap one another; the stated concrete cases came from examining the saved raw and final text. Do not present the zero action failures as a claim that all V2 reply bugs are gone.

This is **implemented and isolated-tested**, not deployed or observed in Telegram. The bounded wording recognizer cannot prove every possible natural-language paraphrase, and the synthetic transport cannot prove card visibility. Other fleet findings remain separate: invented spoken item prices, two other grounding false positives, and unsupported explanations after uncertain reference checks. This candidate does not claim to repair them. The live baseline and settings need a fresh read before any release, and rollback must preserve chats, ownership, purchases and price configuration. No schema change is needed for this candidate.

## Jesse's standing development instructions

For every Twin V2 recommendation or edit, inspect the current code, relevant prompts and recent changes first. Check how the proposed change interacts with existing behaviour before implementing it.

Make the smallest necessary change. Do not add contradictory instructions, duplicate handlers, competing logic, unnecessary prompt layers or extra AI calls. Update the existing responsible component wherever practical.

Keep the bot’s prompt and displayed prompt consistent with what the code actually does. Preserve previously approved behaviour except where the requested change explicitly modifies it.

Test the affected flow and relevant failure cases. Check data compatibility and rollback when applicable. Explain what changed, what was verified and any remaining uncertainty. Never claim there are no clashes without checking.

Work one agreed stage at a time. These are development instructions; keep them outside the bot’s fan-facing prompt.

Apply these requirements to suggestions as well as implementation. Do not recommend or add a change until you have checked it against existing prompts, code and pending work for contradictions, duplicate logic and failure risks.

# Shared reply outcomes repair: isolated candidate

This extends draft PR #7 after its 464-case action replay. It is not a production deployment.

## Baseline and evidence

At 2026-10-13T11:04:53Z both live containers still used source `2f24f023c0cf46bea1c3b3b334458cf1a5df265e` and image `sha256:dff48242b35b94e7b0e757ee4b7778a11958ef85b231b5fdb369542902e325f9`. All 17 current V2 profiles matched the frozen fleet evidence. Release branch remains `2b59d900bd61fbcd335228f2032c6548b37535a1`; PR #7 head before this change is `3bdc81fecdb50c120c0b65967649b41f97778e47`. No pending grounding PR #1 code was merged. Live read-only evidence: `jesse98/twin-dashboard`, branch `codex/v2-card-model-validation-v2-20261013`, `docs/reply-repair-live-baseline.json`.

The earlier report's four empty-final flags need a correction: three actual cards had lost captions. Riley's fourth flag was the deliberately rejected send, whose empty delivered reply is expected. The original flag/result files remain unchanged. The earlier replay had five item-price assertions; three other price flags were generic conversion guidance. Failed reference/ownership checks also produced invented explanations, including assumed visibility or inability to resend unlocked.

## Responsible changes

- `src/grounding.ts`: extend the existing bounded reply validator to remove observed item-price assertions while retaining general Stars conversion and spending/tip conversation. The card remains the price authority. Scope the additional pronoun-based visibility/ownership wording to a content turn, and preserve conditional troubleshooting and freshly verified ownership.
- Fix the two grounding false positives in the same component: a recalled fan refusal is not a stock denial; `red plaid bikini` supports `red bikini` (not blue). This does not relax visual grounding for unsupported descriptions.
- `src/turn.ts`: when all selected-card prose is removed, its existing final fallback supplies a brief neutral introduction instead of a blank caption. The selected file, action, price and actual transport outcome remain unchanged. The existing automatic alternative explanation still takes precedence and survives cleanup.
- A scoped exact-reference verification failure uses the existing honest unavailable line, without inventing a reason. Its existing model selection is restricted to none. An absent reference still permits a clarifying reply. There is no second selector, model call or cleanup pass.
- Optional tip wording now follows the existing none-only discussion/failed-reference schema. Direct fan tips and eligible ordinary tip invitations retain their existing paths.
- Replace existing shared prompt sentences in place for brief captions, failed verification and payment certainty. Snapshot v12 explicitly checks each intended replacement. Runtime and dashboard use the same shared renderer; creator voice/emoji variables are unchanged.

## Isolated verification

The saved pre-edit regression is `reply-outcomes-baseline.json`: 191 checks, 57 failed assertions. The current suite adds six scope boundaries and sixteen prompt/schema checks, passing 213 checks. It uses the saved model replies, real turn/queue/delivery paths and synthetic transport on ordinary and Business routes. It checks exact file and price, one model call, supported descriptions, honest failed-read responses, conditional troubleshooting, ordinary conversation and retained alternative disclosure.

All 24 offline suites passed in the recorded gate. Typecheck passed. The final optional-tip consistency line is followed by focused reply/reference/tip verification. The first candidate regression run exposed three conversion false positives caused by an escaped regular expression; that expression was corrected, not the conversion assertions. Two older grounding assertions intentionally expected a blank caption; they now require the precise neutral caption and still assert the original selected file and locked state. The prompt-length gate increased only to accommodate the reviewed in-place wording; the exact snapshot replacement checks and original upper-size gate remain.

The next real-model fleet replay must use this exact source, the same original histories/catalogues, fresh profile/runtime guards, one call per turn and fake Telegram. It must preserve original failed results and review heuristic flags rather than count every numeric conversion or rejected transport as a bug. No repeated unchanged replay to obtain a pass.

## First fleet replay and evidence-driven amendment

The first reply candidate `a3f1571f219a0e45eba40dd1aa7ba58713a0f633` completed 464 cases / 464 calls across all 17 V2 profiles. Its action and new nonempty-caption/failed-reference assertions passed, and every profile's preview/render output agreed. Runtime and settings were unchanged. Original result: `reply-outcomes-first-model.json`, workflow 38389545420. **This was not an all-reply pass.**

# Shared Twin V2 photo/reply repair — deployment record

13 October 2026, Brisbane time.

**Implemented, tested and deployed.** The authorised release completed at **16:43:51 Brisbane**. All **16 active V2 creators** were verified running it. A read-only follow-up at 16:44 confirmed the same image/source, current settings and fleet, with no pending handovers.

## Exact release

- Production source/merge commit: `2f24f023c0cf46bea1c3b3b334458cf1a5df265e`.
- Tested product source: `5e789f1d23bf63f91643760537600c077b646356`; later changes through the merge add evidence only.
- Both bot and dashboard image: `sha256:dff48242b35b94e7b0e757ee4b7778a11958ef85b231b5fdb369542902e325f9`.
- PR: https://github.com/jesse98/twin-sexbot/pull/6
- Full remote tree: 255 files, reconstructed from the guarded remote base; 251 packaged files verified byte-for-byte in each running container. Four historical archive files are deliberately excluded by the existing Docker ignore rules.
- Only 11 intended source/test/package files were copied to the host. Four are runtime files: media, turn, grounding and the shared template. No partial local snapshot replaced the remote tree.

The five repairs are in shared components used by current and future V2 creators: truthful eligible remaining availability and scoped new-photo selection; generic different/new wording excluded from visual attributes; natural genuine-alternative captions; bounded evidence-based stock/file/delivery validation; and complete-sentence cleanup. [The isolated-stage record](shared-photo-repair-stage.md) explains the exact changes, regression coverage and limits.

## Verification

- **23 packaged offline suites plus TypeScript passed** on the exact release image.
- **39/39 real-model cases in 39 calls** passed on source `5e789f1`, using the frozen real incident histories/catalogue and the existing conversation-model call. Model tests were not rerun during deployment.
- Original baseline **22/62 failures** and initial candidate **35/39** results remain preserved. The earlier release's historical 49/50 result is unchanged.
- Both ordinary and Business routes were covered in isolated tests. Current-fleet prompt and price checks covered all 16 active V2 profiles; real-model creator cases covered Riley, Kyla, Mrs Callace and Briana.
- At **16:43:05**, the running dashboard HTTP root and Riley details endpoint returned 200; all 16 displayed photo/Stars sections matched the actual renderer, preview/render parts matched, and per-creator settings, emoji policies and pricing matched the saved baseline.
- After releasing the handovers, all 16 creators were observed running; settings/model/provider order and source image were checked again.
- The bounded natural-traffic observation recorded **8 Business turns** across Alanna, Kyla, Riley and Trashy: Telegram acknowledged six text replies and **2 Riley photo cards**, with 0 invalid selections and 0 local delivery errors in that sample. No new exact-resend event was observed in this short window; its regression evidence remains isolated.
- This observation sent no test/fan messages, made no purchases and added no model calls.

Telegram acknowledgments are delivery receipts, **not proof that the fan can see the card**. Actual visibility in Jesse's Telegram chat remains unverified. These samples do not guarantee every future natural-language response.

## Deployment interruption and remaining dashboard issue

The first authorised attempt passed both containers' 251-file checks, then the dashboard root HTTP check timed out at **16:36:52**. The controlled rollback completed at **16:37:46**, with all 16 creators running the preceding `86b0ad1` / `9649329` image and settings unchanged. No chat or financial snapshot was restored. That failed attempt is retained in [the attempt-one record](shared-photo-repair-deployment-attempt1.json).

At **16:39**, root and Riley-details timeouts were reproduced on that restored old image. The dashboard showed about 95% CPU while the bot showed about 2%. This established an existing monitor availability problem; its exact cause is not fully diagnosed here.

The reviewed second attempt kept the tested product image unchanged. The actual HTTP prompt/price checks were moved into the held/drained rollout window, with one same-image dashboard recovery when it was unresponsive. All prompt/price comparisons still had to pass before releasing the creators; they did pass. Runtime, fleet and settings checks also passed after release.

**The monitor timeout recurred in the 16:44 follow-up and remains unresolved.** It is explicitly reported separately from the passed core release checks. This record does not claim that every live health check passed. Dashboard source and the all-time history feature were not modified by this repair.

## Compatibility and rollback

The current 16-creator fleet was discovered and preserved: alanna-pow, allison-parker, bethany-marquez, briana-redd, cat-chase, dakota-lyn, dreka-cakez, fit-sid, kyla-yesenosky, mrs-callace, olivia-jade, riley-mae-lewis, tammy, toochi, trashy, tru-kait. Other active/paused/legacy assignments were not changed. Current approved settings hash remains `6872fc74c61d508c1cb193fc53d452a6040303419ba50cb94a3cb5a7b52016a2`.

Five-Star photo pricing remains scoped to tester 6814483810 for Riley, Kyla and Trashy as already deployed. Normal fans and other creator scopes retain normal pricing. Exact-file resend, fresh ownership checks and unlocked owned-photo delivery are covered by the regression suites. No schema or persisted-state format changed. There was no history reset, purchase restoration, bulk recaptioning, video expansion, feature activation or creator migration in this release.

Exact preceding image and source are retained at:
`/home/ubuntu/twin-v2-backups/shared-photo-baseline-5e789f1-1791872165074291746`.

The guarded rollback restores only the changed code/configuration and preceding pinned images, after draining the current checked fleet. Chats, purchases, financial records and creator assignments are excluded from restoration. The first attempt exercised this rollback successfully. The reviewed current command is recorded in [the deployment receipt](shared-photo-repair-deployment.json); recheck source/settings before using it if subsequent work occurs.

The diagnostic workflow entry is now read-only; future diagnostic pushes do not repeat a deployment or model replay.

## Jesse's standing instructions — retain verbatim in every handoff

For every Twin V2 recommendation or edit, inspect the current code, relevant prompts and recent changes first. Check how the proposed change interacts with existing behaviour before implementing it.

Make the smallest necessary change. Do not add contradictory instructions, duplicate handlers, competing logic, unnecessary prompt layers or extra AI calls. Update the existing responsible component wherever practical.

Keep the bot’s prompt and displayed prompt consistent with what the code actually does. Preserve previously approved behaviour except where the requested change explicitly modifies it.

Test the affected flow and relevant failure cases. Check data compatibility and rollback when applicable. Explain what changed, what was verified and any remaining uncertainty. Never claim there are no clashes without checking.

Work one agreed stage at a time. These are development instructions; keep them outside the bot’s fan-facing prompt.

Apply these requirements to suggestions as well as implementation. Do not recommend or add a change until you have checked it against existing prompts, code and pending work for contradictions, duplicate logic and failure risks.
